newsitem.title: USA: N.J. gov challenger vows no tax increases -- paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. gov challenger vows no tax increases -- paper.

text.p: U.S. Rep Robert Andrews Tuesday vowed he would not raise taxes for four years if successful in his bid to unseat Gov Christine Whitman in November, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Wednesday.
Andrews, a Democrat who has won the endorsement of former Gov. Jim Florio, said the Republican incumbent's policies have forced large increases in property taxes during her tenure.
Whitman administration officials said property taxes have risen at the slowest rate in 20 years.

Andrews also blasted Whitman's plan to borrow $2.9 billion as part of a proposal to fully fund the state's pension system. He said the plan was fiscally irresponsible, noting in particular that it includes $647 million of one-shot budget revenue raisers that will have to be replaced in future years.
An administration official said Whitman has cut reliance on one-shots to about $300 million annually, compared to $1.5 billion under Florio.
